forces.title: Stablecoins replace slow cross-border interbank settlement
forces.description: Stablecoins and tokenized commercial bank deposits are increasingly used as highly efficient wholesale settlement tools, particularly in illiquid or currency-constrained B2B corridors. They operate alongside instant payment networks to replace slower correspondent interbank settlement, fundamentally altering the infrastructure for cross-border corporate treasury flows.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Digital assets bypass traditional payment economics
forces.description: Digital assets, including stablecoins and tokenized deposits, could pose a significant headwind to traditional payments and deposit revenues. They bypass conventional interchange and foreign-exchange conversion markups, and shift float income away from commercial bank deposits, leading to direct margin pressure on FX spreads and correspondent banking fees for incumbent providers.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Emergence of digital-asset-based settlement models
forces.description: A new wave of innovation in cross-border payments involves digital-asset-based settlement models. Stablecoins offer an alternative for transferring value across borders, while tokenized deposits facilitate instant settlement within and between financial institutions via interoperable tokenized networks. These are currently relevant for treasury, wholesale, and niche use cases.
forces.source_title: Cross-border payments: Out of the commodity trap, into the future

forces.title: AI agents optimize transactions via digital asset rails
forces.description: Autonomous software agents are expected to dynamically route transactions based on cost, speed, and trust. This could shift the competitive edge to players enabling agent-directed routing across multi-rail environments, including digital asset networks, leading to increased adoption and optimization of transactions through stablecoins and tokenized assets for businesses and consumers.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Tokenized treasury products drive corporate cash yield seeking
forces.description: Corporate treasurers are increasingly shifting excess cash into tokenized treasury and cash-equivalent products to earn yield on idle balances. This trend, accelerated by agentic AI, will require banks to compete for deposits traditionally held due to inertia, posing a risk to conventional deposit profit pools and driving demand for tokenized assets.
forces.source_title: The decade to redefine UK banking

forces.title: Bank of England supervisory focus on regulated stablecoins
forces.description: The Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA) of the Bank of England has made innovation in deposits, e-money, and regulated stablecoins a supervisory priority. This regulatory attention is crucial for the legitimate scaling and integration of digital assets into the financial system, shaping governance and monitoring issues for fast-moving agentic workflows and tokenized products.
forces.source_title: The decade to redefine UK banking

forces.title: Regulatory fragmentation hinders payment rail innovation
forces.description: National supervisory frameworks are viewed as a primary pacing variable for payment rail innovation. Instead of converging, major markets pursue paths to preserve monetary sovereignty, leading to regulatory divergence. This fragmentation creates challenges for cross-border transactions, particularly for autonomous, AI-initiated execution, impacting the scalability of new digital asset networks.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Shift to multirail orchestration with digital assets
forces.description: The payments industry is seeing a shift in advantage from owning specific payment rails to intelligently orchestrating an increasingly fragmented infrastructure. This includes domestic real-time payment systems, card networks, and new settlement mechanisms such as stablecoins and tokenized deposits, enabling providers to offer global cross-border capabilities without building proprietary infrastructure for every market.
forces.source_title: Cross-border payments: Out of the commodity trap, into the future

forces.title: Lagging stablecoin adoption in card-resilient markets
forces.description: Markets like the United Kingdom, North America, and Western Europe are 'card-resilient,' meaning they possess mature credit and debit card infrastructure. Entrenched merchant acceptance, high-value consumer rewards, and built-in dispute resolution preserve the card perimeter, causing stablecoins and local A2A rails to lag significantly in adoption projections through 2035.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

viewpoints.title: Stablecoins and tokenized deposits are efficient wholesale settlement tools, not retail currencies
viewpoints.description: Two-thirds of executives view stablecoins and tokenized commercial bank deposits as highly efficient tools for wholesale settlement, particularly in illiquid or currency-constrained B2B corridors. They are seen as replacing slow correspondent interbank settlement rather than serving as consumer-facing retail currencies, indicating a specific market application focus for these digital assets.
viewpoints.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

viewpoints.title: Digital assets to pose headwinds for traditional payment and deposit revenues
viewpoints.description: McKinsey analysis suggests digital assets like stablecoins and tokenized deposits could create headwinds for traditional payment and deposit revenues if they scale. This is because stablecoins can bypass traditional interchange and FX markups, and shift float income away from commercial bank deposits, directly impacting margin pressure for cross-border corporate corridors adopting tokenized settlement.
viewpoints.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

viewpoints.title: UK and Western Europe to see marginal stablecoin adoption by 2035
viewpoints.description: In 'card-resilient markets' like the United Kingdom and Western Europe, card and wallet adoption is projected to remain very high through 2035. Conversely, stablecoins and local account-to-account (A2A) rails are expected to lag significantly, indicating limited mainstream consumer adoption for stablecoins in these mature markets compared to traditional payment methods.
viewpoints.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

viewpoints.title: Bank of England identifies regulated stablecoins as supervisory priority
viewpoints.description: The Bank of England’s Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA) has marked innovation in deposits, e-money, and regulated stablecoins as a supervisory priority. This indicates a heightened regulatory focus on these digital assets, suggesting a move towards formal frameworks that could legitimize and integrate them into the broader financial system, albeit under strict oversight to manage risks.
viewpoints.source_title: The decade to redefine UK banking

viewpoints.title: Digital asset settlement models are emerging for specific use cases, broader adoption pending
viewpoints.description: Stablecoins and tokenized deposits are noted as emerging digital-asset-based settlement models that offer an alternative for cross-border value transfer and instant settlement. While currently relevant for treasury, wholesale, and niche applications, broader adoption of these models is still anticipated in the future, indicating ongoing development and potential for wider market integration.
viewpoints.source_title: Cross-border payments: Out of the commodity trap, into the future

demand_drivers.description: Stablecoins and tokenized commercial bank deposits are viewed by executives as highly efficient for wholesale settlement, particularly in illiquid or currency-constrained business-to-business corridors, replacing slower interbank settlement.

Stablecoins offer an alternative mechanism for transferring value across borders, promising instant settlement within and between financial institutions through interoperable tokenized networks, especially in major currency corridors.

Tokenized treasury products enable corporate treasurers to earn yield on idle cash, and automate sweeping idle balances to higher-yield accounts, providing an alternative to traditional bank deposits.

pnl_drivers.driver: Margin pressure on traditional FX and correspondent banking fees
pnl_drivers.description: Adoption of tokenized settlement in cross-border corporate corridors leads to direct margin pressure on foreign-exchange spreads and correspondent banking fees, as stablecoins bypass traditional interchange and FX conversion markups.

pnl_drivers.driver: Shift of float income from commercial bank deposits
pnl_drivers.description: Stablecoins and tokenized deposits shift float income out of commercial bank deposits, impacting banks' net interest income and requiring them to compete for deposits that historically remained due to inertia.

market_sizing.methodology: The document discusses the emerging role of stablecoins and tokenized deposits as wholesale settlement tools and treasury products, rather than providing explicit market sizing. Their relevance is identified in cross-border corporate corridors, illiquid/currency-constrained B2B flows, and corporate treasury for yield optimization.
market_sizing.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world
